title: An Octopus Guarded Her Eggs for 4.5 Years Without Eating

scenes.text: One octopus guarded her eggs for four and a half years.
Scientists found her forty-five hundred feet down, near Monterey, California.
She seemed to never eat the whole time.
She guarded about one hundred sixty eggs.
No animal has ever been recorded brooding eggs for longer.
Then the eggs hatched. She died soon after, her job done.

description:
A deep-sea octopus guarded her eggs for about 53 months, nearly four and a half years, the longest brooding period ever recorded for an animal.
Scientists tracked her 4,500 feet down off California. She apparently never ate.
Would you wait that long?
first_comment: Bonus: she apparently never ate, and about 160 eggs hatched when she was done. Is this the most dedicated parent in nature?
